questions.stem: Cartographer Kate's projection asks why a worker leaving the labor force lowers the unemployment rate

answer.exemplar: When a worker stops searching, they leave both the labor force and the unemployed count, so the unemployment rate falls even though no job was found.

questions.explanation: Exit removes one from unemployed and labor force, lowering the rate. The idea that jobs were found confuses exit with hiring.
questions.hint: Exit lowers both numerator and denominator.

questions.stem: Cartographer Sam's projection asks what Okun's law implies for policy

questions.explanation: Lower unemployment needs output growth. The idea that small demand changes suffice ignores the coefficient.
questions.hint: Output must grow to cut unemployment.
